transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-05-03 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees (Redwood): Nina Patel (AE), Marcus Liu (SE), Ava Gomez (Solutions Eng)
- Attendees (BlueCrest): Ethan Rivera (Head of Cloud Partnerships), Sofia Mendez (Platform Arch), Liam O'Connor (BD), Priya Shah (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Intro and partner program overview; BlueCrest describes reseller and managed onramp business.
- Discussed integration patterns: hosted API resell, dedicated capacity (reserved), private VPC onramp, recommended auth & billing flows.
- Security checklist: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, data residency options.
- Technical topics: containerized Redwood Private, KV cache/latency, batching, quantization, model variants and routing, fallback when capacity constrained.
- Agreed next steps: share partner pricing and integration diagram, technical deep-dive on private deployment + KMS.

Topics mentioned:
- Partner program, reseller margins, marketplace listing, onboarding flow
- VPC peering, private control plane, on-prem appliance
- KMS/HSM integration, key rotation, BYOK, audit logs
- Autoscale policies, burst capacity, latency SLOs, continuous batching
- Model pinning, rollouts, canary, A/B, fallback routing

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect at times):

[00:00] Nina Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Nina from Redwood - I'll run a quick agenda, then Marcus will jump into the tech bits. How's everyone doing?

[00:08] Ethan Rivera: Doing well, thanks - excited to chat. We've been talking internally about a partner onramp for enterprise customers that want GPU-backed inference without managing infra.

[00:16] Nina Patel: Great. BlueCrest, we've read your partner deck, but tell us more about the three customer profiles you mentioned - resell through channel, managed service, and pure on-prem.

[00:28] Sofia Mendez: Sure - the majority now are managed onramp: we bake an image and provide GPU capacity plus ops. Some want pure on-prem because of data residency; others want marketplace quickstarts. We're exploring embedding Redwood as a backend option.

[00:40] Marcus Liu: Thanks. From Redwood's side we have three deployment models that map well: hosted API where you call our REST endpoints, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads. In partner mode we can support reseller flows or a direct integration where BlueCrest hosts Redwood Private inside your customer's VPC.

[00:58] Liam O'Connor: Quick commercial question: can partners get a special reseller rate or white-labeled API? We need margins for our managed services.

[01:06] Nina Patel: Yes, our partner program has reseller pricing tiers based on commit; we'll share the one-pager. Typically discounts are tied to committed capacity or annual contracts. We'll also outline marketplace fee splits if you list as a managed offering.

[01:20] Priya Shah: On security, first pass: we need SOC2, TLS everywhere, SAML SSO for customer admin, audit logs retained for 1 year, and ideally KMS/BYOK for encryption at rest. Do you support HSMs?

[01:32] Marcus Liu: Good callouts. Redwood supports BYOK via customer-managed KMS; HSM integrations are available for Private installs. For hosted we provide envelope encryption and strong access logging. I will send the security checklist.

[01:44] Sofia Mendez: A couple of tricky cases: some customers require strict egress controls and cannot have outbound connections from compute units; we need an air-gapped option.

[01:52] Marcus Liu: We have an on-prem package that can be fully air-gapped. Deployment is a private control plane you run; we can also provide an appliance image. There are some trade-offs: automatic model catalog updates aren't available in air-gapped mode, and kernel or quantization updates would be manual.

[02:12] Ethan Rivera: Talking about model updates - how do you handle model pinning and rollouts? We want to guarantee stability for a customer's critical flows.

[02:19] Marcus Liu: We support version pinning at the route level - you can pin to a model variant or quant profile. Rollouts support canary and A/B with traffic split. There's a fallback routing policy: if the pinned model isn't available, we can failover to a compatible variant that meets latency or cost SLOs.

[02:36] Nina Patel: From a go-to-market lens, we want to understand the onboarding flow: do BlueCrest sales bring customers to Redwood for onboarding, or do you want to white-label?

[02:44] Liam O'Connor: We prefer to own the customer experience for managed services. For reseller or marketplace customers, we could refer.

[02:50] Ava Gomez: Operationally, a common integration is that BlueCrest consumes our hosted API and resells it. That path is quickest but less differentiated. The deeper integration is embedding Redwood Private in BlueCrest's onramp to bundle both infra and the inference runtime - that gives you more margin and control.

[03:06] Priya Shah: Two more security specifics: do you provide per-customer audit logs that we can ingest? And can we integrate with our SIEM?

[03:14] Marcus Liu: Yes, Redwood exposes audit logs per tenant; we support S3-compatible exports and a webhook for log streaming. SIEM integration is common; we'll include sample connectors.

[03:26] Ethan Rivera: Great. On the technical side, performance is key - our managed customers want <100ms p95 for short chat prompts and consistent throughput. How do you guarantee latency?

[03:36] Marcus Liu: We operate a GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching, KV cache, and optimized kernels. For low-latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated pools sized to expected qps with strict autoscale policies. For some workloads we suggest prefix caching and quantized model variants to reduce cost. There's always a tradeoff: aggressive batching improves hardware utilization but can increase tail latency.

[03:58] Sofia Mendez: Does Redwood support dynamic routing so we can route tenant traffic across regions or model variants based on latency/cost?

[04:06] Marcus Liu: Yes, smart routing policies are supported - you can route by latency, cost preference, or tenant tier. We have automated fallback rules when a region or model is unconstrained.

[04:16] Liam O'Connor: For your Dedicated capacity, do you allow bursting to public pools if reserved is saturated? That helps us smooth usage.

[04:25] Nina Patel: We offer configurable burst policies: you can allow limited burst to hosted capacity with cost controls and automatic fallback. That way the customer maintains availability while preserving predictable baseline cost.

[04:36] Priya Shah: On compliance: any certifications beyond SOC2? Do you have ISO or data residency controls?

[04:44] Marcus Liu: We have SOC2 Type II. ISO is on the roadmap; for data residency we support region pinning and Private deployments inside customer-managed VPCs for strict residency requirements. We'll share the compliance matrix.

[04:58] Ethan Rivera: One integration detail: BlueCrest wants to surface usage and cost back into our billing system and also provide customers with token-level cost breakdowns. Is usage metering available per-tenant and per-route?

[05:09] Marcus Liu: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token- and route-level metrics. For partners we can surface APIs or push billing exports to your system on a schedule. We'll include the export schema.

[05:22] Sofia Mendez: Curious about the model side - can we onboard custom customer models or must customers use the Redwood catalog?

[05:29] Marcus Liu: Private supports customer-supplied models; hosted can host customer models in dedicated accounts or via bring-your-model on dedicated capacity. For air-gapped, you'd have to bring the model artifacts into the environment manually.

[05:42] Nina Patel: A brief commercial note — pricing varies by model size, quantization, and deployment type. We'll send a sample pricing grid. Partners on reserved commits get the best effective cost.

[05:52] Liam O'Connor: How much engineering effort to get a standard integration live for managed customers? We need an estimate to pitch to prospects.

[05:58] Marcus Liu: For a hosted API reseller integration, timeline can be 2–4 weeks including SSO and billing hooks. For Private embedding into an onramp with KMS and air-gap considerations, expect 6–10 weeks depending on compliance checks and infra readiness. These are rough estimates.

[06:18] Ethan Rivera: Does Redwood support testing and benchmarks before committing? We want to run a perf run vs our current stack and GoliathCloud.

[06:25] Marcus Liu: Yes, we can run a benchmarking exercise. We'll provide a lightweight harness and can run a small-scale perf test on Dedicated or Private. We'll need representative prompt sets and sequence length distributions.

[06:36] Priya Shah: On keys and encryption, key rotation policies? We require quarterly rotate and immediate revocation if a key is compromised.

[06:44] Marcus Liu: BYOK workflows include rotation and revocation APIs; for Private you can enforce your own KMS policies. We'll document the process.

[06:54] Nina Patel: Are there any blockers you see from a partner onboarding perspective?

[07:00] Sofia Mendez: Main blockers: clearly defined reseller economics, quick technical checklist for customers, and a secure way to provision keys into customer environments. Also legal — we need sample contract language for data processing.

[07:12] Nina Patel: We'll loop in legal and partner ops. We'll send a standard MSA template and partner addendum for review.

[07:20] Ethan Rivera: Awesome. A few more clarifications — do you support SAML provisioning for customer admins and SCIM for user sync?

[07:28] Marcus Liu: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for both hosted and Private. For air-gapped Private we provide SAML artifacts to host locally.

[07:36] Liam O'Connor: For managed customers, what's the observability story? We need traces and per-call latency breakdowns for troubleshooting.

[07:44] Ava Gomez: Redwood Console provides per-route latency, token breakdown, traces, and error analysis. We can also supply tracing hooks to push spans to your tracing backend.

[07:56] Priya Shah: Any special network ports or firewall rules? Our infra team will want a checklist.

[08:02] Marcus Liu: We'll provide a network diagram and a list of outbound endpoints required for hosted and Private. For on-prem and air-gapped, the checklist differs — we'll produce both.

[08:12] Nina Patel: Great — sounds like a fit for experimentation. For the immediate next steps: Marcus will send the integration diagram and API contract; I'll send partner pricing one-pager and partner program details; Priya will send security questions. Then we'll schedule a technical deep-dive for the Private install.

[08:30] Ethan Rivera: Happy with that — can we get the initial docs by early next week?

[08:34] Nina Patel: Yes - Marcus and I will get the main artifacts out by Friday (2028-05-05).

[08:40] Sofia Mendez: One small ask: sample SLA for Dedicated pools and example canary rollout policy.

[08:46] Marcus Liu: We'll attach the SLA and a sample rollout policy doc.

[08:52] Liam O'Connor: Cool. Any final questions?

[08:56] Priya Shah: Nothing else from me; just the security checklist.

[09:00] Nina Patel: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the items. Meeting end.
